items.q: There's smoke pouring out of my apartment's hallway, what do I do
items.pred: Call 911 (or your local emergency number) as soon as you're outside. Get out now and take everyone you can; don't stop for belongings, and don't go back in. If there's smoke, stay low and crawl. Feel doors with the back of your hand before opening; if a door is hot, use another way out. If you're trapped, close the door, block the gap under it with a towel, and signal from a window while you call.

items.q: My toddler swallowed a bunch of pills from my purse

If they're awake and alert, US Poison Control (1-800-222-1222) can also help.

items.q: My wife is having a seizure on the floor
items.pred: Call 911 (or your local emergency number) now. Move hard or sharp things away and put something soft under their head. Don't hold them down and don't put anything in their mouth. Time the seizure; when the shaking stops, roll them onto their side and stay with them until they're fully awake. If they aren't breathing normally once it stops, start CPR.

items.q: A man at the bus stop is bleeding a lot from his leg
items.pred: Call 911 (or your local emergency number) now. Press firmly on the wound with a clean cloth or your hands and don't let up. If blood soaks through, put more cloth on top and keep pressing; don't lift the first layer. For a badly bleeding arm or leg, a tourniquet 2 to 3 inches above the wound can help if you have one. Keep them lying down and warm until help arrives.

items.q: Grandma suddenly can't lift her arm and her words come out slurred
items.pred: Call 911 (or your local emergency number) now, even if the signs seem to fade. Note the time the symptoms started and tell the dispatcher, because treatment depends on it. Don't give them food, drink, or medicine, including aspirin. Keep them comfortable, and if they get drowsy or vomit, lay them on their side.

items.q: My son is choking and can't breathe
items.pred: Call 911 (or your local emergency number) now, or have someone call while you help. If they can cough hard, let them keep coughing. If they can't cough, speak, or breathe, stand behind them, put a fist just above the belly button, and pull sharply in and up until the object comes out. For a baby under 1, give 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades, then 5 chest pushes with 2 fingers, and repeat. If they pass out, start CPR.

items.q: My baby isn't breathing
items.pred: Call 911 (or your local emergency number) now and put the phone on speaker. Check if the child is breathing: watch their chest for up to 10 seconds. If they're not breathing normally, start CPR if you can (for a baby, press with 2 fingers in the center of the chest; for a child, use the heel of one hand), about 2 pushes a second, and the dispatcher will coach you. Stay with them until help arrives.
